Parent checks cover existence, deletion, and lock status but omit institute and course relationship authorization.

independentFinding.impact: ICS membership can currently authorize access to foreign, inaccessible, or course-linked KX parents without the persisted relationship required by the revised design.
independentFinding.recommendation: Implement a shared parent-resolution boundary that constrains KxPost by ICS institute and, when course-linked, by approved enrollment, instructor assignment, or eligible ADMIN authority. Resolve answers and comments through that authorized post before any mutation or private response.

independentFinding.title: Current staff checks grant institute-wide mutation authority without explicit moderator or course relationship checks

sourceEvidence.explanation: Any normalized ADMIN or INSTRUCTOR passes the staff check after an unscoped answer lookup.
Any normalized ADMIN or INSTRUCTOR can delete the comment without resolving course assignment or an explicit moderator relationship.
The endpoint performs institute-wide analytics reads after KX eligibility alone and has no KX_MOD role check.

independentFinding.impact: Students may reach private analytics, while instructors can mutate course-linked content outside their assignments. This violates the revised KX_MOD role and persisted-relationship boundary.

Keep course-less board moderation limited to the explicitly defined ICS moderator roles.

independentFinding.title: Comment creation can persist two unrelated parents

sourceEvidence.explanation: The handler rejects only when both parent identifiers are absent; it does not reject when both are present.
postId and answerId are validated independently without proving that the answer belongs to the supplied post.
Both identifiers are written to KxComment, allowing unrelated parent references.

independentFinding.impact: A comment can be attached simultaneously to unrelated post and answer records, making authorization, deletion authority, visibility, and notification semantics ambiguous and enabling cross-resource association.
independentFinding.recommendation: Require exactly one parent identifier, or atomically resolve answerId through its post and require any supplied postId to match. Apply institute/course visibility authorization to the resolved canonical post before creation.

independentFinding.title: Answer state mutations and gamification/notification effects are not consistently atomic or idempotent

sourceEvidence.explanation: Acceptance state and notification are transactional, but EXP is awarded afterward and errors are swallowed; repeated acceptance requests can repeatedly invoke the award helper.
Verification, EXP award, and notification are separate operations with swallowed failures; repeat requests can re-trigger side effects.
The answer count is blindly decremented when soft-deleting, with no demonstrated nonnegative or concurrency-safe transition predicate.

independentFinding.impact: Retries, concurrent requests, or partial failures can produce duplicate EXP, missing notifications, inconsistent verification effects, or incorrect answer counts despite a successful response.
independentFinding.recommendation: Implement transition-based, idempotent side effects keyed to the answer and transition, and place coupled database changes in one transaction. Update/delete with predicates that prove the prior state, and emit EXP/notification only when the intended state transition actually occurs.

independentFinding.title: Current shared role normalization converts SUPER_USER and every unknown role into STUDENT

sourceEvidence.explanation: Only ADMIN and instructor aliases are recognized; every other role is returned as STUDENT.
Every assigned handler obtains its role through the unsafe normalizer.
Eligibility is then based on the session user's institute and returns the normalized role, so an ICS SUPER_USER can reach handlers as a STUDENT unless an individual handler happens to require staff.

independentFinding.impact: The unimplemented baseline cannot enforce the revised UNKNOWN fail-closed rule or the mandatory SUPER_USER 403 ceiling across the assigned KX operations.
independentFinding.recommendation: Implement an explicit recognized-role result including SUPER_USER and UNKNOWN, make UNKNOWN unauthorized, and require every assigned handler to reject SUPER_USER/UNKNOWN before protected parsing, reads, writes, serialization, notifications, EXP, or other effects.

independentFinding.title: Current handlers do not consistently enforce persisted course visibility and parent-child binding

sourceEvidence.explanation: A flag is created directly from caller IDs without resolving the selected answer/comment/post to an accessible parent post.
GET checks only the actor-owned follow row and does not establish that the requested post or tag is visible and valid for the actor.
POST resolves only post existence/deletion and does not enforce course-linked enrollment, instructor assignment, or Admin authority.
The parent post is resolved without its course/institute relationship before answer creation.
A caller-supplied courseId is added directly to the feed query without first proving enrollment, assignment, or Admin course authority.
courseId, syllabusItemId, and tagIds are persisted without resolving their mutual relationship or the actor's course authority.

independentFinding.impact: Recognized ICS users may read or mutate course-linked KX resources outside their enrollment or assignment, create mismatched course/syllabus links, or attach flags/follows to inaccessible resources.
independentFinding.recommendation: Implement the revised KX capability as persisted, query-constraining parent resolution before effects. Resolve all child IDs through the authorized post/course, enforce approved enrollment or instructor assignment/Admin authority, and return a uniform safe 404 for foreign or mismatched resources.

independentFinding.title: Current moderation operations grant institute-wide staff access without target-course assignment checks

sourceEvidence.explanation: Authorization stops at normalized ADMIN or INSTRUCTOR role.
The transaction updates caller-selected post, answer, or comment IDs and writes an audit row without first resolving the target's actual parent, ICS author, or instructor course assignment.
Any eligible normalized instructor or Admin receives global pending flags and recent actions, including reporter email and content, with no target-course authorization constraints.
Any normalized INSTRUCTOR is treated as staff and may delete any selected post, without checking course assignment or the distinct course-less-board moderation rule.

independentFinding.impact: An ICS instructor can moderate, deanonymize, inspect reporter data, or delete course-linked content outside courses they teach. Caller-supplied postId in the moderation audit can also be unrelated to an answer/comment target.
independentFinding.recommendation: Resolve each moderation target to its actual post, course, and author before returning private queue data or mutating. Require assignment for course-linked content, apply the explicit course-less-board rule, constrain Admin eligibility as designed, and derive audit postId from the resolved target rather than accepting an unrelated value.

independentFinding.title: Current detail GET mutates viewCount before proving resource visibility or existence

sourceEvidence.explanation: The handler increments viewCount immediately from postId and suppresses update errors before loading and authorizing the post.
The not-found/deleted decision occurs only after the attempted mutation.

independentFinding.impact: Requests for deleted, foreign, or otherwise unauthorized posts can cause a persistent side effect before the required safe 404 and relationship decision.
independentFinding.recommendation: Resolve the post through an authorization-constrained query first. Increment viewCount only after successful visibility authorization, and ensure denied or absent resources produce no effects.

independentFinding.title: Current answer and post creation trigger gamification outside the authorization/write transaction

sourceEvidence.explanation: Answer creation and notification commit first; EXP is then attempted through a separate helper and errors are suppressed.
Post creation commits before the separate EXP helper runs, and helper errors are suppressed.

independentFinding.impact: Once relationship authorization is added, stale or incompletely authorized state can still feed a separate global helper; partial success also leaves effects inconsistent and complicates verification that all effects occur only after the authorized parent boundary.
independentFinding.recommendation: Bind gamification to the already-authorized actor and resolved parent, define the intended atomicity/idempotency contract, and ensure no EXP path can re-resolve an unauthorized or mismatched resource.

independentFinding.title: Current role normalization maps unknown and SUPER_USER values to STUDENT

sourceEvidence.explanation: Every role other than ADMIN or an instructor alias falls through to STUDENT.
KX routes consume normalizeRole and return that result without an explicit recognized-role or SUPER_USER rejection.

independentFinding.impact: Until implemented, KX routes can interpret SUPER_USER or malformed role values as STUDENT, contrary to the revised UNKNOWN fail-closed and hard legacy ceiling contract.
independentFinding.recommendation: Implement a canonical role resolver with explicit SUPER_USER and UNKNOWN results, then require an allowed normal role at every assigned protected entry before parsing inputs, protected reads, writes, or side effects.

independentFinding.title: KX search and voting do not enforce persisted parent visibility and course relationships

sourceEvidence.explanation: Search constrains posts to non-deleted ICS records but does not constrain course-linked posts by the actor's approved enrollment, instructor assignment, or Admin authority.

Vote target lookup reads only authorId, voteCount, and deletion state; answers are not resolved through their parent post, and neither target is checked for institute, course visibility, enrollment, or assignment.
Vote mutations and author EXP effects execute after the incomplete target checks.

independentFinding.impact: Before implementation, recognized ICS actors may search or vote on course-linked content without the required persisted course relationship, and unauthorized mutations can trigger vote-count and gamification effects.
independentFinding.recommendation: Resolve each post, and each answer through its parent post, with institute/status/deletion and course membership predicates before returning content or entering the mutation transaction. Keep vote ownership bound to the canonical actor and perform EXP only after the authorized committed vote result.

independentFinding.title: Material annotation operations lack student-role, enrollment, institute, and material-parent authorization

sourceEvidence.explanation: GET checks only for a session and filters annotations by attachmentId and userId; it does not resolve Attachment to SyllabusItem and Course or validate STUDENT role and APPROVED enrollment.
POST accepts an attachmentId and creates an annotation for the session user without resolving or authorizing the attachment's actual material, course, institute, or enrollment.
DELETE verifies annotation ownership but does not resolve its attachment and course boundary or require the MATERIAL policy's student enrollment relationship.

independentFinding.impact: Until implemented, authenticated non-students and students without access to the underlying course material can reach annotation reads or writes, and SUPER_USER is not explicitly denied before protected processing.
independentFinding.recommendation: At each method entry enforce canonical STUDENT role, then resolve annotation/attachment through SyllabusItem and Course with matching actor institute and APPROVED enrollment. Use uniform safe 404 for foreign or inaccessible parents and deny SUPER_USER/UNKNOWN before parsing protected identifiers.

independentFinding.title: Material completion grants gamification effects without MATERIAL authorization

sourceEvidence.explanation: The handler obtains a generic workspace session, parses a caller-selected syllabus item ID, and reads the item without checking STUDENT role, MATERIAL type, course institute, or APPROVED enrollment.
The handler grants EXP and evaluates a badge using the unverified item and caller-supplied duration.

independentFinding.impact: Any authenticated session, including SUPER_USER or a user unrelated to the course, may trigger material EXP and badge effects for an arbitrary syllabus item until the design is implemented.
independentFinding.recommendation: Deny SUPER_USER/UNKNOWN and non-STUDENT actors before parsing; resolve an actual MATERIAL syllabus item through its course, actor institute, and APPROVED enrollment before any completion, EXP, badge, notification, or study effect.

independentFinding.title: Own-notification and avatar routes do not enforce the Super User legacy ceiling

sourceEvidence.explanation: Any authenticated session reaches request parsing and a success response; no allowed-role or SUPER_USER denial exists.

independentFinding.title: Push-token registration is only an echo and subscription state is process-local

sourceEvidence.explanation: The handler echoes the submitted token and deviceType without validation, ownership-bound persistence, or an actual registration effect.
Subscription state is held in a module-local Map.

independentFinding.recommendation: During implementation, define the actual owned subscription/token persistence contract, validate endpoint/token/device data, bind records to actor and device identity, and make deletion target only an owned record. If these endpoints are intentionally placeholders, document and verify their no-registration semantics rather than returning misleading success.

independentFinding.title: Baseline account routes do not enforce the revised role ceilings and relationship rules

sourceEvidence.explanation: Both methods accept any authenticated session; no explicit recognized-role check denies SUPER_USER or UNKNOWN before reads, parsing, or writes.
The route parses and updates preferences for any authenticated session and returns the full updated user object without a normal-role ceiling.

The target user and extensive profile relations are read before authorization; authorization checks only institute equality and does not require self, Admin, or a persisted shared-course relationship.

independentFinding.impact: Until implemented, SUPER_USER/UNKNOWN actors can reach unsupported account routes, and arbitrary same-institute profiles can be disclosed before the revised PROFILE_READ relationship is enforced.
independentFinding.recommendation: Implement the canonical actor resolver and explicit normal-role guard before protected parsing or reads. For third-party profiles, constrain the initial query to self, Admin, or a persisted shared-course relationship and return a uniform safe 404 for unauthorized targets.

independentFinding.title: Baseline study-session routes do not enforce student role or persisted course/item relationships

sourceEvidence.explanation: POST accepts caller courseId and syllabusItemId, creates the log, then grants EXP and checks badges without verifying STUDENT role, approved enrollment, same institute, or that the item belongs to the course.
GET filters actor-owned logs by caller courseId but does not enforce current enrollment or institute relationship.

independentFinding.impact: An authenticated unsupported role, including SUPER_USER, can invoke study effects, while a student can bind logs and gamification effects to unauthorized or mismatched course resources.
independentFinding.recommendation: Before parsing protected inputs or effects, enforce recognized STUDENT role. Resolve non-null course and syllabus item through one approved enrollment and same-institute parent chain, reject mismatches with safe 404, and only then create the log or trigger gamification.

independentFinding.title: Baseline todo route lacks an explicit student-role and home-institute guard

sourceEvidence.explanation: The route accepts any authenticated session, resolves a caller-selected institute, and enumerates that actor's enrollments without verifying STUDENT role or matching the institute to the actor's persisted home institute.
An unauthorized course filter returns 403 rather than the revised uniform safe 404, and response construction exposes course and instructor metadata.

independentFinding.impact: SUPER_USER/UNKNOWN or other non-student actors are not denied at entry, and the error contract can reveal whether a requested course falls outside the actor's enrollment set.
independentFinding.recommendation: Apply canonical authentication, recognized STUDENT role, and persisted home-institute equality before institute/course reads. Constrain course selection through approved enrollment and return the required uniform safe 404 for unavailable or unauthorized course targets.

independentFinding.title: Baseline upload route permits unsupported roles and publishes unbound content

sourceEvidence.explanation: Only session presence is checked before multipart parsing; there is no recognized-role ceiling or explicit SUPER_USER/UNKNOWN denial.
Files are published as public Blob URLs, public filesystem paths, or transferable data URLs without actor ownership metadata.

independentFinding.impact: Until the revised design and the separate handoff contract are implemented, unsupported actors can consume storage and publish content, and subsequent attachment operations cannot prove ownership of returned upload references.
independentFinding.recommendation: Deny SUPER_USER/UNKNOWN before multipart parsing, validate a recognized normal role, and implement the revised actor-bound staging mechanism before returning an attachable reference.

independentFinding.title: Baseline workspace handlers do not explicitly deny SUPER_USER or UNKNOWN

sourceEvidence.explanation: All methods rely on requireWorkspaceSession and contain no local recognized-role or explicit SUPER_USER/UNKNOWN denial; event reads and mutations also use institute scope rather than the revised ownership/course authority.
Ownership predicates exist for reads and mutations, but no method locally enforces the revised normal-role ceiling before protected parsing/read/write.
Ownership predicates exist for task records, but no explicit normal-role ceiling is present and courseId is accepted without relationship validation.

independentFinding.recommendation: Implement a canonical WORKSPACE guard at every method entry that validates active authentication, recognized normal role, and persisted institute before parsing or database access. Then apply operation-specific ownership and linked-course predicates, including the revised event-read and task-link rules.

independentFinding.title: Canonical role handling required by the design is not implemented in supplied shared policy

sourceEvidence.explanation: The baseline role normalizer maps every unrecognized value, including SUPER_USER and malformed roles, to STUDENT.
Shared guards consume the unsafe normalizer; requirePermission may grant a non-Admin unknown/SUPER_USER actor based on stored permissions, contrary to the hard legacy ceiling.
Session validation establishes active identity but does not implement the revised explicit role classification or operation capability.

independentFinding.impact: Reusing baseline normalization or permission helpers during implementation can silently confer STUDENT behavior or stored permission capabilities on SUPER_USER/UNKNOWN, defeating route-specific denial rules across this subset.
independentFinding.recommendation: Introduce and consistently use a fail-closed role classifier that returns explicit UNKNOWN and SUPER_USER values. Keep the managed-role normalizer limited to validated ADMIN/INSTRUCTOR/STUDENT inputs, and prohibit persisted permissions from overriding the SUPER_USER legacy ceiling.

independentFinding.title: Public leaderboard baseline may disclose users who have not opted in

sourceEvidence.explanation: The public query filters role, activity, and active status but does not filter GamificationProfile.publicLeaderboardOptIn.
The model includes publicLeaderboardOptIn, demonstrating an existing persisted public-disclosure control.

independentFinding.impact: Because U-01 preserves this endpoint as anonymous and unchanged, the current implementation can publish a student's identity or pseudonymous stable identifier despite an opt-out value. This is a known baseline exposure, not a defect introduced by the revised Super User design.
independentFinding.recommendation: Track this under the existing public-leaderboard privacy contract and remediate only through the separately authorized U-01/public scope; do not add Super User-specific optional authentication behavior here.

independentFinding.title: Production metadata trust and revocation operations remain unassigned

sourceEvidence.explanation: The supplied document explicitly leaves the trusted academic/privacy approver, manifest maintainer/release reviewer, production dataset ID/fingerprint and attestation procedure, expiry lifetime, and revocation owner/runbook as required human or operator assignments.

independentFinding.impact: Deny-by-default permits safe non-deployment, but trustworthy production disclosure cannot begin until accountable identities, the production dataset binding, expiry policy, and publication/revocation procedure exist. No reviewer may invent those assignments.
independentFinding.recommendation: Before production deployment, obtain and record the named governance assignments and dataset attestation procedure through the authorized human process. Continue withholding all oversight results while any required assignment or valid manifest is absent.

independentFinding.title: Admin course actions do not yet implement the revised canonical actor and complete relationship boundary

The baseline uses separate institute lookup, course lookup, deletion, and revalidation; the revised implementation remains absent.

independentFinding.impact: Until implemented, role/alias handling, instructor-target validation, actor binding, and side-effect ordering do not satisfy the revised design; create may also leave a course persisted if downstream assignment fails.
independentFinding.recommendation: Implement the final adjudicated action policy with the canonical request actor, persisted institute/course/target-instructor predicates, safe not-found behavior, and atomic or explicitly compensating dependent writes before revalidation.

independentFinding.title: getInstructors currently exposes instructor identities without authentication

sourceEvidence.explanation: The exported server action performs institute and user reads without calling ensureAdmin or any other authentication/authorization boundary and returns IDs, names, and emails.

independentFinding.impact: Direct invocation can enumerate instructor identity and email data for a caller-selected institute, including by unauthenticated, SUPER_USER, UNKNOWN, or ordinary-role callers.
independentFinding.recommendation: Authenticate at action invocation, require the final ADMIN policy, resolve the institute server-side under that authority, and return a safe denial before institute or user reads.

independentFinding.title: Four createTemplate actions authenticate presence only and do not bind actor, course, or institute

sourceEvidence.explanation: The action checks only for any session, then creates an ActivityTemplate using closure courseId and session user ID without TEACH role, assignment, institute, or ICS checks.
The action checks only session presence and parses attacker-controlled configuration before creating against the closure courseId, with no persisted course authorization.
The action parses JSON before any relationship check and accepts every authenticated role for a write to the closure courseId.
The action checks only session presence before creating the template and issuing cache/redirect effects.

independentFinding.impact: Compiled-action replay permits authenticated students, foreign instructors, SUPER_USER, or other unsupported roles to create templates in unrelated courses; closure values and prior page rendering do not provide authorization.
independentFinding.recommendation: At the first action boundary, resolve the canonical actor, reject unsupported/SUPER_USER/UNKNOWN roles, resolve an active ICS course by both courseId and route institute, require instructor assignment or ADMIN authority, and perform all checks before parsing, writing, revalidation, or redirect.

independentFinding.title: Template editor reads before authorization and saveTemplate permits unscoped cross-course writes

sourceEvidence.explanation: The page reads an ActivityTemplate by templateId before authenticating or checking its course and institute relationship, and serializes its fields into the form later in the page.
The action requires only any session and parses submitted JSON without TEACH authorization.

independentFinding.impact: Direct page access can disclose template content, and compiled-action replay can create or modify templates and linked syllabus titles across course or institute boundaries, including by students or SUPER_USER.
independentFinding.recommendation: Guard the page before its first template read. Independently guard action replay by resolving the canonical actor, course, template, and syllabus item through one persisted TEACH-authorized parent chain; reject mismatches safely before parsing or effects and apply the adjudicated atomicity contract.

independentFinding.title: Assigned page guards do not yet enforce persisted course authorization or the complete instructor alias set

sourceEvidence.explanation: The render guard accepts INSTRUCTOR, PROFESSOR, and ADMIN based only on session role, omits TEACHER, and does not resolve the course, assignment, or institute.
The render guard has the same role-only behavior, alias omission, and missing persisted parent binding.
The render guard has the same role-only behavior, alias omission, and missing persisted parent binding.
The render guard has the same role-only behavior, alias omission, and missing persisted parent binding.

independentFinding.title: Inline template creation currently authenticates but does not enforce the designed course, institute, role, or assignment boundary

sourceEvidence.explanation: The replayable inline action checks only that a session exists, then creates an ActivityTemplate using the closure courseId and authenticated user ID. It does not re-resolve the course or require a teaching role, instructor assignment, actual institute, or ICS eligibility before mutation and redirect.

independentFinding.impact: Any authenticated legacy actor, including a student or SUPER_USER, could replay the compiled action and create a template in a supplied/closed-over course.
independentFinding.recommendation: Implement invocation-time canonical actor resolution and deny unsupported roles before parsing. Resolve the closure courseId to an ICS course and require instructor-alias assignment plus matching home institute, or ADMIN authority, before creation, revalidation, or redirect.

independentFinding.title: Broadcast implementation does not bind the supplied institute code to the authorized course

sourceEvidence.explanation: The action authenticates and checks course ownership/Admin status, but the course query selects no institute and the authorization check does not bind instituteCode to the persisted course institute.
The untrusted instituteCode is embedded into recipient notification links and revalidation paths after authorization.

independentFinding.recommendation: Resolve the actual course institute during authorization, enforce instructor home-institute matching, and construct links/revalidation paths only from the persisted supported institute code. Recognize all canonical instructor aliases and deny SUPER_USER before form parsing.

independentFinding.title: Classwork-item actions lack required role, enrollment, parent-course, institute, and child-identity enforcement

sourceEvidence.explanation: The helper accepts any authenticated role, and getOrCreateSubmission reads or creates by a supplied syllabusItemId without resolving its course, institute, or APPROVED enrollment.

Ownership checks are limited to submission.studentId. Caller-supplied courseId, itemId, and instituteCode are not matched to submission.syllabusItemId or its persisted course before grading side effects and cache invalidation.
After checking ownership of the supplied submissionId, the action deletes attachmentId directly without proving that the attachment belongs to that submission.

The grading actions accept PROFESSOR/Admin based only on role and update an arbitrary submissionId without resolving the submission through an instructor-assigned/Admin-authorized course and actual institute.

independentFinding.impact: Existing actions permit cross-course creation, mutation, attachment deletion, grade changes, gamification, badge, and revalidation effects. SUPER_USER is not consistently denied, and legitimate aliases/enrolled-student requirements are not enforced.
independentFinding.recommendation: Implement the revised canonical actor resolver at every export. Resolve SyllabusItem→Course and Submission→SyllabusItem→Course, enforce STUDENT plus APPROVED enrollment and ownership for student work, enforce instructor alias assignment/home institute or ADMIN for grading, bind all supplied route IDs to the persisted chain, and require attachment.submissionId to equal the authorized submission before any read or effect.

independentFinding.title: Syllabus actions do not enforce institute and nested-resource membership required by the design

sourceEvidence.explanation: The helper checks course instructor equality or ADMIN but does not enforce recognized instructor role, instructor home institute, actual route institute, or early SUPER_USER denial.
Caller-provided group IDs and attachment metadata are inserted without proving the groups belong to the authorized course or that attachment artifacts are authorized for that actor/course.

The action authorizes supplied courseId but deletes supplied itemId without verifying item.courseId equals the authorized course.

independentFinding.recommendation: Resolve the actual course and institute before effects; require instructor-alias assignment with matching home institute or ADMIN. For update/delete, resolve itemId through that course. Validate every target group against the same course and every attachment against the authorized upload/parent contract before mutation, then derive revalidation paths from persisted institute data.

independentFinding.title: Gradebook actions currently rely on role-only checks and permit cross-course reads, writes, exports, and incentives

Require canonical instructor assignment and matching home institute or ADMIN, resolve submissions/items/students through that course with approved membership, scope incentive rules to that course, and place the authorization before Promise.all, executeSkill, mutations, notifications, gamification, and export construction.

independentFinding.title: People actions do not consistently bind enrollment, comment, group, member, and institute resources to the authorized course

sourceEvidence.explanation: The shared helper checks course instructor equality/Admin but not a recognized instructor role, instructor home institute, persisted institute code, or early SUPER_USER denial.

independentFinding.recommendation: Resolve one canonical actor and actual course/institute at each export. Enforce instructor alias assignment/home institute or ADMIN, prove every enrollment/group belongs to the course and each target student is an appropriate enrollment member, authorize private-comment reads and recipients through that relationship, require the callable enrollment service to reauthenticate and revalidate actorId, and derive revalidation paths from persisted institute data.

independentFinding.title: Required production metadata-governance identities and dataset/revocation procedures remain unassigned

sourceEvidence.explanation: The supplied document explicitly states that the trusted academic/privacy approver, manifest maintainer/release reviewer, production dataset identity/fingerprint and attestation procedure, expiry lifetime, and revocation owner/runbook require human or operator assignment.

independentFinding.title: Announcement actions do not yet enforce the revised actor, institute, and persisted-parent contract

sourceEvidence.explanation: Current code uses the legacy session and caller-provided instituteCode; the course lookup omits instituteId. Although create checks instructor ownership, it does not bind the supplied institute route to the persisted course.

Require assigned instructor alias or ADMIN under TEACH, reject SUPER_USER/UNKNOWN before protected reads, and derive revalidation scope from the authorized persisted parent.

independentFinding.title: Course mutation actions retain role-only or incomplete relationship authorization

sourceEvidence.explanation: The shared legacy guard checks only exact role strings and does not apply canonical aliases, UNKNOWN fail-closed handling, actual institute binding, or operation-level relationships.
Creation trusts caller instituteCode and creates a course without assigning the authenticated instructor despite the revised creation contract.
These actions verify course/institute equality but do not require instructor ownership for non-Admin PROFESSOR actors.
These mutations update solely by caller courseId after a role check, with no persisted ownership or institute predicate.

independentFinding.impact: NOT_REMEDIATED baseline exposure: an authenticated instructor can mutate foreign or unassigned courses, while canonical INSTRUCTOR aliases can be incorrectly denied. Caller-selected institute codes can also drive creation and cache effects.
independentFinding.recommendation: Implement the revised TEACH/create capability at every export, bind instructor creation to the actor's persisted institute and actor.id, resolve mutation targets with course institute and instructor predicates, and derive revalidation paths from authorized persisted scope.

independentFinding.title: Student and card actions do not yet bind actor institute, role, and every target row

sourceEvidence.explanation: Current requestEnrollment never resolves the course or verifies its institute against the student's persisted institute before creating enrollment.
Current code compares the course to a caller-selected instituteCode but never proves that institute is the authenticated student's home institute.
Current discovery has no STUDENT role check and trusts caller instituteCode, allowing any authenticated role to enumerate another institute's course and instructor metadata.
Unenrollment does not resolve course institute or require an APPROVED actor-owned enrollment; reorder trusts caller isStudent and does not establish role or eligibility for every supplied course ID.

independentFinding.impact: NOT_REMEDIATED baseline exposure: cross-institute enrollment attempts and catalog disclosure remain possible, and arbitrary card targets can be written without the revised per-row relationship checks.
independentFinding.recommendation: After correcting the enrollment-entry design finding, implement canonical authentication and persisted actor-institute checks. Resolve every course and enrollment through actor-bound predicates, infer student/instructor behavior from the authenticated role rather than isStudent, and reject the whole reorder request if any row is unauthorized.

independentFinding.title: Callable skill exports currently lack real invocation authentication

sourceEvidence.explanation: The exported use-server function performs assignments without resolving any authenticated actor; input instituteId controls tenancy checks.
The function grants Admin authority by looking up caller-supplied input.actorId rather than binding it to the real request actor.
The function authorizes using caller-supplied actorId and does not authenticate the invocation.
The public server action performs random generation and collision database reads without any actor or capability check.

independentFinding.impact: NOT_REMEDIATED baseline exposure: direct server-action invocation can impersonate an Admin or instructor, mutate course/user/enrollment data, disclose generated credentials, or probe course-code collisions. SUPER_USER denial is not established at these direct boundaries.
independentFinding.recommendation: Reauthenticate at the first statement of every exported use-server entry, bind any actorId to the canonical actor, deny SUPER_USER/UNKNOWN before parsing or reads, and enforce the operation-specific ADMIN/TEACH/creation relationship contract using persisted institute and parent records.

independentFinding.title: Bulk ingestion still maps unknown roles to STUDENT and exposes non-cryptographic temporary passwords

sourceEvidence.explanation: Role input is passed through normalizeRole, whose supplied shared-policy source maps every unrecognized value to STUDENT; passwords are generated with Math.random.
The raw temporary password is returned in each successful record.

independentFinding.impact: NOT_REMEDIATED baseline exposure: malformed, UNKNOWN, or SUPER_USER-like role input can silently provision a granted STUDENT account contrary to the revised fail-closed provisioning contract, and weak credential generation increases account-compromise risk.
independentFinding.recommendation: Use an explicit provisioning-role allowlist that rejects unknown/SUPER_USER values, use a cryptographically secure password or activation mechanism, and constrain credential delivery to the separately authorized Admin workflow without logging it.

independentFinding.title: Bulk-user creation and its required audit are not atomic

sourceEvidence.explanation: User creation commits in one transaction, then createAuditLog writes through the global database client afterward. Audit failure therefore leaves created accounts without the expected audit record.

independentFinding.impact: NOT_REMEDIATED baseline exposure: privileged account creation can succeed without its corresponding audit evidence, weakening accountability and leaving the caller with an ambiguous failed skill result after durable mutations.
independentFinding.recommendation: Perform authorized user creation and the audit insert in one interactive transaction using tx only, or explicitly define and review a durable compensating/outbox contract. Do not call the global createAuditLog helper from inside the transaction.

independentFinding.title: Bulk assignment and enrollment management do not fully enforce revised roles and target relationships

sourceEvidence.explanation: Current validation omits the INSTRUCTOR alias, does not authenticate Admin authority or instructor self-assignment, and permits assigning any accepted target instructor once caller instituteId matches.

Authorization does not require an instructor-alias role or matching instructor home institute; auto-process updates every pending enrollment without validating each target student's role and institute.
Manual processing checks enrollment.courseId but not the target student's role/institute relationship required by TEACH.

independentFinding.impact: NOT_REMEDIATED baseline exposure: caller-controlled identities can reassign instructors or approve unrelated/invalid members, and persisted course ownership alone can accidentally confer authority on an actor with an invalid role.
independentFinding.recommendation: Require canonical authenticated role plus relationship, validate actor and target instructor/student active roles and institutes, bind every child to the authorized course, and keep all validation and writes within an atomic transaction where batch semantics require it.

independentFinding.title: Required production metadata-governance identities and dataset bindings remain unassigned

sourceEvidence.symbol: META-01 exact disclosure and operational contract
sourceEvidence.explanation: The supplied revised design explicitly states that the trusted academic/privacy approver, manifest maintainer/release reviewer, production dataset ID/fingerprint and attestation procedure, expiry owner/lifetime, and revocation publication owner/runbook are required human or operator assignments and are not supplied.

independentFinding.impact: NOT_REMEDIATED operational blocker: no production metadata approval can be trusted or bound to the actual production dataset, and expiry/revocation publication cannot be operated. The design's deny-by-default rule must therefore withhold all production oversight DTOs; deployment cannot truthfully enable disclosure.
independentFinding.recommendation: Before production enablement, humans/operators must assign the institution-designated approver, independent manifest maintainer/reviewer, production dataset identity and fingerprint attestation procedure, approval lifetime owner, and revocation publication/runbook owner. Keep the manifest absent or invalid and all oversight reads denied until those assignments and reviewed entries exist.

independentFinding.title: Current group-permission action trusts caller-selected course and student identifiers

sourceEvidence.explanation: The current action performs membership and syllabus queries from supplied courseId and studentId without authenticating an actor, binding studentId to that actor, resolving approved enrollment, or validating instructor assignment and institute.

independentFinding.impact: Any caller able to invoke the server action can enumerate group membership and syllabus visibility across courses, including as SUPER_USER or UNKNOWN.
independentFinding.recommendation: During authorized implementation, add the revised canonical actor, role, institute, enrollment/assignment, and persisted-parent checks before these queries, with uniform safe foreign-resource handling.

independentFinding.title: Current sentiment server action is unauthenticated

sourceEvidence.explanation: The exported use-server action accepts content and computes a result without resolving a session or rejecting SUPER_USER, UNKNOWN, inactive, or unauthenticated callers.

independentFinding.impact: The server-action surface remains publicly callable outside the recognized legacy-role boundary and could become a more serious escape if its pluggable implementation later gains external or protected-data effects.
independentFinding.recommendation: During authorized implementation, authenticate at invocation, require a recognized active legacy role, deny SUPER_USER and UNKNOWN before processing content, and preserve legitimate callers.

independentFinding.title: Current gradebook service exports student identities and grades without authorization

sourceEvidence.explanation: The service immediately runs course, approved-enrollment, syllabus-item, and submission queries from caller-supplied courseId, including student names, email addresses, and grades, without authenticating or validating assignment, institute, or ADMIN authority.
The queried private roster and grade data is serialized into a downloadable CSV response.

independentFinding.impact: A direct caller can export a foreign course's roster, email addresses, assessment titles, and grades; SUPER_USER is not denied before the protected queries.
independentFinding.recommendation: During authorized implementation, authenticate inside the callable service entry and resolve the actual course before Promise.all; permit only an assigned same-institute instructor alias or ADMIN, deny SUPER_USER/UNKNOWN, and constrain every enrollment, item, and submission through that course.

independentFinding.title: The skills barrel exposes unguarded callable boundaries and converts failures to untyped results

sourceEvidence.explanation: The shared wrapper catches all errors, logs messages, and returns an untyped failure without preserving authorization status.
The assigned actions and gradebook service are re-exported from the common skills entry point, making their current unguarded behavior available to programmatic callers.

independentFinding.impact: Direct or barrel-based invocation reaches the same unimplemented authorization boundaries, while wrapper behavior can obscure whether a real authorization denial occurred.
independentFinding.recommendation: Keep authorization mandatory inside every callable export regardless of import path, and implement the revised explicit authorization-failure contract consistently at the shared wrapper boundary.

affectedAC: Header-free page, shell and RSC protection
independentFinding.title: Common dashboard layout currently performs legacy reads and effects before any SUPER_USER shell branch

sourceEvidence.explanation: Current implementation derives legacy institute scope before any explicit SUPER_USER branch.
Activity and Knowledge Exchange eligibility services are invoked before shell selection.
Legacy enrollment/course titles and codes are queried before rendering the shell.
Login-reward processing and gamification reads precede the existing DashboardLayout render.

independentFinding.impact: Until implemented, a SUPER_USER request can enter legacy eligibility, course, gamification, and shell preparation rather than receiving the isolated AcademicOperationsShell. This is an unimplemented baseline exposure, not a defect in the revised design.
independentFinding.recommendation: Implement the specified canonical-session and supported-institute checks, then branch on explicit role before every legacy read or effect. Pass SUPER_USER only the approved oversight DTO and basic own identity to a dedicated shell.

affectedAC: Header-free page, shell and RSC protection
independentFinding.title: Current course layout reads private course data before complete role, institute, and relationship authorization

sourceEvidence.explanation: The layout reads the course, instructor name, and pending-enrollment count using courseId alone before authorization.
The current check does not explicitly reject SUPER_USER or unknown roles and does not bind the course query to the route institute.
Pending submission counts are queried after only the incomplete instructor/Admin classification.

independentFinding.impact: Until implementation, a SUPER_USER assigned as instructor, an unrecognized role with enrollment, or a cross-institute course identifier may reach legacy course data and derived counts.
independentFinding.recommendation: Apply the revised design literally: recognize only the canonical normal-role set, deny SUPER_USER/UNKNOWN before private reads, resolve Course with both courseId and actual institute, and establish instructor assignment, approved enrollment, or Admin authority before counts, headers, tabs, or children.

affectedAC: Header-free page, shell and RSC protection
independentFinding.title: Sandbox remains an unguarded client page with hard-coded submission identities

sourceEvidence.explanation: The existing page is a client component and therefore cannot perform the required server-leaf authentication itself.
The page is described as dev-only and defines hard-coded student and assignment identifiers.
Those hard-coded identifiers are passed to SubmitBar, exposing a mutation-capable flow to caller-controlled client execution.

independentFinding.impact: Until the planned extraction is implemented, direct navigation can load the client activity and attempt submissions using identities that are not bound to the authenticated actor or persisted authorized template/course relationship.
independentFinding.recommendation: Create the specified server wrapper at the existing page path, reject SUPER_USER/UNKNOWN before rendering, extract current UI into the allowlisted legacy-client component, and ensure every submission API independently binds the real actor, institute, template, course, enrollment, and owned attempt.

affectedAC: Header-free page, shell and RSC protection
independentFinding.title: Existing shared shell components fall unknown and SUPER_USER roles into legacy Admin or Student navigation and mount forbidden widgets

sourceEvidence.explanation: The existing dashboard always mounts Sidebar, Topbar, and MobileBottomNav for every supplied role.
Any role other than instructor aliases or ADMIN falls back to Student links, so SUPER_USER and UNKNOWN currently receive student navigation.
Any role other than Student or the two recognized instructor aliases receives Admin tabs.
Only Student and PROFESSOR/TEACHER are distinguished.
The fallback selects Admin items, exposing account, permission, and audit-log navigation to SUPER_USER/UNKNOWN.
The legacy topbar mounts search, settings, and NotificationBell controls.
The legacy user menu exposes profile, settings, privacy, help, and logout rather than the exact Super User support surface.

independentFinding.impact: Until the separate oversight shell is implemented, role fallbacks can present legacy Student/Admin affordances, notifications, profile/settings links, search, and other features explicitly excluded from the Super User contract. UI links are not authority, but they expand exposure and bypass the intended least-privilege shell.
independentFinding.recommendation: Never pass SUPER_USER or UNKNOWN into the legacy DashboardLayout component tree. Implement a dedicated AcademicOperationsShell containing only approved scope selection, oversight navigation, own basic identity, and logout; also make legacy role selection fail closed for defense in depth and include the INSTRUCTOR alias where normal-role behavior requires it.

affectedAC: Header-free page, shell and RSC protection
independentFinding.title: Current institute landing page has no SUPER_USER redirect and displays an unknown-role response

sourceEvidence.explanation: Only STUDENT, PROFESSOR/TEACHER, and ADMIN are redirected; all other roles receive the Unknown role JSX response.

independentFinding.impact: Until implemented, an authenticated SUPER_USER visiting an institute root does not reach that institute's academic-operations destination, and the INSTRUCTOR alias also lacks its intended normal-role redirect.
independentFinding.recommendation: After canonical authentication and supported-institute validation, redirect SUPER_USER to the same requested institute's academic-operations route, retain the stated ICS initial-login behavior at the login destination, map the canonical INSTRUCTOR alias to the instructor landing, and fail UNKNOWN closed without private props.

affectedAC: Header-free page, shell and RSC protection
independentFinding.title: Middleware currently treats cookie presence as sufficient routing assistance and omits Bearer-only page requests

sourceEvidence.explanation: The middleware checks only whether lumina_session is present; it neither validates the session nor recognizes a Bearer credential for page routing.
All cookie-bearing requests continue regardless of token validity, confirming that server leaves must remain the final authority.

independentFinding.impact: Stale or forged cookie values reach server routes, while a Bearer-only page request may be redirected. The revised design correctly removes middleware from final authority, but this baseline remains until server leaves consistently authenticate and the desired routing compatibility is implemented.
independentFinding.recommendation: Keep middleware non-authoritative as designed. Ensure every assigned server layout/page uses the canonical cookie-first, Bearer-fallback resolver and does not depend on middleware admission; preserve or explicitly implement Bearer-compatible routing assistance if page access is part of the transitional contract.

independentFinding.title: Production disclosure remains intentionally blocked by unassigned operational trust and dataset controls

sourceEvidence.symbol: META-01 exact disclosure and operational contract / Operational decisions
sourceEvidence.explanation: The supplied document explicitly leaves the trusted academic/privacy approver, manifest maintainer/release reviewer, production dataset identity/fingerprint and attestation procedure, approval lifetime, and revocation publication owner/runbook as required human or operator assignments.

independentFinding.impact: No production metadata approval can be trusted or admitted until these identities and procedures are assigned. Under the specified deny-by-default behavior, the exact blocking effect is that oversight reads must return the safe METADATA_REVIEW_REQUIRED failure and serialize no DTO; deployment cannot claim usable production disclosure.
independentFinding.recommendation: Before production disclosure, governance must name the institution-designated approver and independent manifest maintainer/reviewer, establish the real production dataset fingerprint and attestation procedure, choose approval lifetimes, and own a coordinated revocation publication runbook. Do not invent these values; retain deny-by-default until supplied.

independentFinding.title: Current bulk assignment action has no authenticated actor or capability check

sourceEvidence.explanation: The exported server action enters executeSkill and begins its transaction without resolving an authenticated request actor or denying SUPER_USER/UNKNOWN callers.

The current implementation trusts input instituteId for course validation and updates Course.instructorId without proving actual ADMIN authority or the designed instructor self-assignment relationship.

independentFinding.impact: Until implemented, a directly invoked server action can read instructor/course records and reassign courses without the revised design's actor, role, institute, and ownership boundary.
independentFinding.recommendation: At action entry, resolve one actual request actor using the canonical session resolver; deny unauthenticated, inactive, SUPER_USER, UNKNOWN, and unauthorized roles before transaction reads. Inside the transaction, bind all predicates to the real actor and persisted course/instructor institutes, allowing only actual ADMIN authority or instructor-alias self-assignment to a course already owned or just created by that actor. Do not treat input instituteId or any claimed actor identity as authority.

independentFinding.title: Current instructor validation omits the canonical INSTRUCTOR alias and exposes internal errors

sourceEvidence.explanation: Only PROFESSOR and TEACHER are accepted, although the revised contract defines PROFESSOR, TEACHER, and INSTRUCTOR as canonical instructor aliases.
Caught exception messages are copied into the action result, which can disclose database or internal implementation details.

independentFinding.impact: A legitimately authorized INSTRUCTOR would regress, while failures may reveal sensitive implementation details to direct callers.
independentFinding.recommendation: Use the revised fail-closed canonical role resolver and include all three instructor aliases. Map unexpected failures to a stable safe action error while retaining detailed diagnostics only in an authorized server-side channel that does not contain rejected metadata.

independentFinding.title: Current permission guard can grant persisted permissions to unrecognized or SUPER_USER roles

sourceEvidence.explanation: After authentication and activity checks, the guard grants ADMIN automatically and grants every other raw role when its persisted permissions JSON contains the requested permission; it does not restrict permission-bearing callers to the managed ADMIN/INSTRUCTOR/STUDENT role set or impose the SUPER_USER ceiling.

independentFinding.impact: Before implementation, a SUPER_USER or unknown raw role with legacy permissions could pass permission-protected legacy operations, contrary to the oversight-only design.
independentFinding.recommendation: Resolve the explicit revised role set first; deny SUPER_USER and UNKNOWN before parsing persisted permissions, retain ADMIN behavior, and permit legacy permission evaluation only for recognized managed normal roles where the specific operation contract allows it.

independentFinding.title: Current reauthentication helper is not bound to the authenticated Admin

sourceEvidence.explanation: The helper accepts an arbitrary adminId, loads that user's password, and compares it without authenticating the caller, checking the target's role/activity, or requiring adminId to equal the real session actor.

independentFinding.impact: A caller that controls adminId can use another account's credentials as reauthentication proof, undermining sensitive Admin operations if its consumer does not independently enforce all missing bindings.
independentFinding.recommendation: Bind reauthentication to the already resolved real active ADMIN session, require the supplied identifier to equal that actor if retained for compatibility, and perform password verification against that same actor within the sensitive operation's authorization flow.

independentFinding.title: Frozen fixture helpers do not yet enforce the revised META-01 value and failure contract

sourceEvidence.explanation: The shape checker validates keys and scalar types but does not require blank course/material descriptions and coverImage, blank announcement content, MATERIAL-only rows, or approval binding for each exact persisted mutable value.
The failure checker allows any nonempty subset of error/message/code with arbitrary strings rather than requiring the fixed METADATA_REVIEW_REQUIRED safe-500 contract.
The audit assertion finds a matching row but does not establish transaction/commit ordering, rollback on audit-write failure, or withholding after ambiguous commit.

independentFinding.impact: Future execution of only these frozen helpers could pass responses that violate META-01 or fail to demonstrate the exact transactional access-audit boundary.
independentFinding.recommendation: Keep this frozen fixture unchanged as required, but add the separately reviewed supplementary cases specified by the revised design for exact approved values, blank fields, MATERIAL-only selection, contamination, expiry/revocation/wrong-dataset changes, exact safe failure, rollback, commit ambiguity, and post-commit serialization ordering.

independentFinding.title: Current schema does not constrain stored role values

sourceEvidence.explanation: User.role is a free-form String with a comment listing only legacy roles; the database does not constrain recognized values and the comment does not include explicit SUPER_USER or UNKNOWN semantics.

independentFinding.impact: Invalid, misspelled, or improperly provisioned role strings remain possible. Safety therefore depends entirely on every application boundary implementing the revised fail-closed resolver and provisioning restrictions.
independentFinding.recommendation: Implement centralized fail-closed application validation at every authentication and role-write boundary, including rejection of SUPER_USER in public/bulk/role-change selection. If a database enum or constraint is later proposed, treat it as a separately reviewed migration rather than assuming this schema already enforces the contract.

independentFinding.title: Production metadata governance and dataset binding remain unassigned

sourceEvidence.explanation: The supplied verification fixture deliberately binds only to a disposable loopback harness database and fixture hash; it cannot identify or attest a production dataset, approver, maintainer, expiry owner, or revocation publisher.

independentFinding.impact: No production metadata may be trusted or disclosed until real governance identities and a production dataset/fingerprint attestation and publication procedure are assigned. The revised deny-by-default rule prevents unsafe admission but makes production oversight unavailable.
independentFinding.recommendation: Before deployment, humans/operators must assign the institution-designated academic/privacy approver, manifest maintainer/release reviewer, production dataset identity and fingerprint attestation procedure, approval lifetime owner, and revocation/publication runbook owner. Continue withholding all oversight results while any assignment or binding is absent or invalid; do not derive production authority from fixture identities.
